package_info.package_manager: Trojan-downloader (Windows malware, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware family, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: Stantinko is a malicious adware/botnet distributed via software bundling, used for browser hijacking, click fraud, and brute-force attacks against Joomla and WordPress sites. Its behavior is intentionally deceptive, unauthorized, and harmful to both end users and web services.

execution_context.file_location: Installed as part of bundled adware (Windows executable, e.g., C:\Program Files\Stantinko\stantinko.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Injected browser extension or process that redirects browser traffic, manipulates search results, and injects ads.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++/JavaScript (native Windows binary with browser manipulation components)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hijacks the user's browser by injecting scripts or modifying browser settings, redirecting traffic and injecting advertisements, resulting in click fraud and potential further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Browser hijacking and ad injection are classic signs of adware and malware, especially when performed without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not alter browser settings, redirect traffic, or inject ads without explicit user permission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Browser extensions may legitimately inject scripts for ad-blocking or UI enhancement, but only with user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Traffic redirection to ad or malicious domains
Bundled installation without clear user consent

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Automated brute-force module targeting Joomla and WordPress admin login pages.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates automated brute-force attacks against Joomla and WordPress sites by sending repeated login attempts over the network, aiming to compromise web admin accounts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated brute-force attacks are a hallmark of botnet and malware activity, not legitimate user behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not attempt to log in to remote web admin panels without user initiation or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may perform similar actions, but only in authorized security assessments.
key_indicators: Automated login attempts to remote web admin panels
Network traffic patterns consistent with brute-force attacks

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs freeware bundled with Stantinko adware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware installation and persistence on the system.

attack_chain.action: Stantinko executes at runtime, hijacking the browser and injecting ads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Click fraud and potential further malware delivery.

attack_chain.action: Stantinko initiates brute-force attacks against Joomla and WordPress sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential compromise of web admin accounts and further botnet expansion.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized browser manipulation and ad injection
Automated brute-force login attempts to Joomla/WordPress sites
Network traffic to known Stantinko C&C infrastructure
file_indicators: Presence of stantinko.exe or similarly named binaries in Program Files
Unexpected browser extensions or DLL injections
Persistence mechanisms in Windows registry or startup folders
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Stantinko C&C servers
High volume of HTTP POST requests to Joomla/WordPress login pages
Traffic to ad fraud or click-fraud domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized browser extensions, injected scripts, or changes to browser settings. Detect high-frequency login attempts to remote web admin panels from user endpoints. Look for known Stantinko binaries and persistence mechanisms on disk and in the registry. Analyze outbound network traffic for connections to Stantinko C&C infrastructure and click-fraud domains.
